title: Microquake surge probe — scratch notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory log for a new microburst pattern we dubbed 'microquake' — many tiny bursts (5–20 reqs) with very short inter-burst gaps (2–20ms) that produce a resonant effect on the KV cache warmup and kernel selection. Goal: identify whether small, high-frequency bursts cause a persistent p99 inflation and whether fractional batching + aggressive KV priming helps.

Context / Motivation:
- We see customers with chat UI autopredict that issue many tiny requests while a user is typing. Conventional burst tests (burst sizes 50+) don't capture the microquake behavior.
- Hypothesis: microquake causes repeated kernel cold-starts or inefficient batch packing which increases tail latency (p95/p99) despite acceptable p50.

Experiment hardware / service config:
- Cluster: dedicated pool (A100-s), 4 GPUs/pod, 2 pods used.
- Model: open-llama-13b (quantized int8 path), kv-cache enabled.
- Serving runtime: runtime v3.9.2 with default kernel-picker.
- Ingress: local load generator on same region, jitter disabled, accurate inter-arrival timing.
- Observability: token-level tracing, per-request trace id, sampling 100% for this run.

Traffic pattern definition (microquake):
- Burst: sequences of 5, 8, 12, or 20 concurrent single-token requests (simulate streaming token-by-token).
- Inter-burst gap: uniformly sampled 2–20 ms.
- Run length: 30 minutes per config.
- Concurrency cap: per-client 64.

Experiment matrix:
1) Baseline: runtime default batching, no priming, batch_timeout=4ms
2) Fractional batching: enabled fractional packing (pack small requests into soft batches), batch_timeout=2ms
3) KV priming: prefill heuristics (prime last-kv slice for context=64) + fractional batching
4) Kernel pin: force 'fast-attn' kernel even for small seq lengths (stress test)

Metrics collected:
- p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (ms) measured per-request (server processing time excluding ingress network)
- overall QPS (requests/sec)
- KV cache hit-rate (per-request), cache-priming latency contribution
- GPU utilization and kernel-switch counts (inferred from traces)

Raw highlights (aggregated after 30m runs):
- Baseline: QPS ~ 1,100; p50 28ms; p95 110ms; p99 230ms; KV-hit 45%
- Fractional batching: QPS ~ 1,250; p50 30ms; p95 95ms; p99 170ms; KV-hit 48%
- KV priming + fractional: QPS ~ 1,200; p50 34ms; p95 80ms; p99 120ms; KV-hit 76%
- Kernel pin: QPS ~ 1,050; p50 26ms; p95 140ms; p99 310ms; KV-hit 43%

Quick interpretations:
- Fractional batching improves packing of micro-requests, raises throughput slightly and reduces mid-tail, but doesn't fully address p99.
- KV priming is the most effective single lever for p99 in this pattern — large jump in KV-hit and dramatic p99 improvement. Suggests much of the tail was due to repeated KV cache misses and repeated attention recomputation.
- Forcing a single kernel (kernel pin) backfired: while p50 remained low, p95/p99 got worse — likely because kernel implementations optimized for long sequences are suboptimal for tiny bursts, and runtime lost dynamic kernel-selection benefits.

Observed behavioral trace examples (anecdotal):
- Pattern: many requests hit empty slot in GPU L2 / KV slice -> runtime blocks while migrating KV pages -> subsequent burst sees eviction penalties.
- I saw repeating sequence where a request would get 10ms extra stall precisely when a small background housekeeping eviction started. Reproducible in ~70% of KV-miss traces.

ASCII sparkline of p99 across configs (30m windows, lower is better):
Baseline:  ▇▆▇▇▆▇▇▆▇▇▆▇▇▆▇  (avg 230ms)
Fractional batching: ▇▆▆▅▇▆▅▇▆▅▇▅▆  (avg 170ms)
KV priming: ▅▅▅▅▅▅▅▅▅▅▅▅▅  (avg 120ms)
Kernel pin: ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇  (avg 310ms)

Immediate takeaways and action items:
- Short term (prod-safe): enable fractional batching for small-payload endpoints by default (feature flag + telemetry). Rollout plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% (monitor p50/p95/p99).
- Medium term: add a KV priming policy for streaming/small-token workloads (heuristic: if average burst size < 25 and inter-burst gap < 50ms, prefill last N KV slices). Needs work to avoid wasted priming on purely sporadic traffic.
- Avoid kernel pinning as a general policy — keep dynamic kernel selection but add better metrics to detect mis-selection.
- Instrument kernel-switch counts in the console (already added GH PR to trace exporter).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How sensitive is the benefit of KV priming to sequence length? I tested for context=64; need runs for 32 and 128.
- Cost tradeoffs: priming increases token work — quantify per-token cost increase vs tail reduction to inform Optimize recommendations.
- Check interaction with different quantization paths (int4 vs int8). We used int8.
- How does this behavior change when bursts are multi-token requests (instead of single-token streaming)?

Planned next experiments:
- Sweep: context lengths [32,64,128], burst sizes [5,12,20], inter-gap [2,20,50ms], run length 20m each. Aim: heatmap of p99 delta for priming vs no priming.
- Simulate multi-client scenario (N clients 10–100) to see collision effects on KV slices.
- Try lightweight priming (only prime top-2 KV slices) to test marginal benefit per-cost.

Notes to self:
- Save traces with tag microquake-2025-02-18 (done).
- Blog idea: "Why tiny bursts are a different beast — microquake patterns and production mitigations" — short internal draft after sweep.

Appendix: quick run commands (local loadgen)
- baseline: ./loadgen --pattern microquake --burst 8 --gap 2-20ms --duration 1800 --batch_timeout 4
- fractional: same with --enable-fractional --batch_timeout 2
- kv-priming: add --kv-prime=64 --prefill=true

End of scratch.

-- Joris
